newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Steady rain seen in Brazil soybean regions - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Steady rain seen in Brazil soybean regions - Somar.

text.p: Rainfall should remain steady in Brazil's key soybean growing regions as two cold fronts move into the center-south, said independent meteorologists Somar.
The rainiest region will be Parana, between December 18th and 19th, while in the centre-west rains will be isolated with most showers falling in the east and south of Mato Grosso.
The south-east will see isolated showers in the late afternoon until December 19th and 20th, when a cold front will cause heavier rains in Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais.
Somar said that last week, high temperatures and the passage of cold fronts over the ocean had provoked heavy showers in the centre and south of Brazil, benefiting soybean growing regions.
But in Parana rains were still very isolated so that total rainfall varied greatly from one area to the next.
In Rio Grande do Sul, up to 60 mm of rain fell in the region of Santa Maria.
Meanwhile the weather remained dry in the rice growing region further south, holding back planting.
